chapter: Billy and De De Pierce, Al Hirt tour
title: Albert Walters on piano; doubling on piano
summary: Met Albert Walters at a West End club with Paul Moore; talk of horn men who double on piano.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you hear him play piano much by the way? Oh, yeah.

Yeah, I worked with him. Him and I were working in that club back in West End. Used to have nightclubs in West End? With the same Paul Moore. I'll tell you what. Albert was. That's where I first met Albert. He was on piano and I was on band. He worked with Paul Moore, his band back then. Back then. First time I met Albert. And he was a good piano player. He still is good, but you don't have no piano with a voice on. He was a wonderful piano player. Yeah, I hardly ever heard him play piano. He was good. Way back then. When I first came to town I'd hear him different jobs.
Like the one they called the Blue Angel now. Oh, yeah, yeah.
From Peace Fountains. Right along in there.
Somewhere along in there. It was a joint where he played piano. But in late years I just haven't heard him play piano. I thought he was, you know. No, he don't bother with it anymore.

But you know, if Morgan was playing with his brass band he could double on piano. That's right. Just like Picks can double. Well, we used to go to, when we were playing at the Hop Club in Morgan City, we had a band

and Tomless Jefferson playing trumpet where one would get off quick playing piano and Tomless Jefferson would get back on horn and Al would get on piano. Yeah, I've never heard Jefferson play the album.
